title: Failover: add trigger evaluation module (thresholds/windows/hysteresis) behind feature flag
author: Jordan Lee
description:
Summary: This PR introduces a standalone trigger evaluation module for regional failover automation. It evaluates standardized health signals over configurable windows using thresholds, hysteresis, and hold-down timers, and produces an auditable decision object ("desired failover mode" + reasons). The module is integrated in a no-op/monitor-only path behind a feature flag so we can ship, observe, and tune before any orchestration is enabled.

Context / Motivation: Recent incidents showed we detect regional degradation late and inconsistently, and we rely on manual heuristics to decide when to fail over. As part of Regional failover automation upgrade (ENG-2844, umbrella ENG-2841), we need a deterministic and testable trigger engine that: (1) is resilient to noisy metrics (hysteresis + multi-sample windows), (2) avoids flapping (hold-down timers), (3) is explainable/auditable, and (4) can be run in "monitor-only" mode while we validate thresholds.

What’s included: 1) Trigger evaluation core: A pure function evaluator that consumes a RegionHealthSnapshot and a TriggerPolicy and returns TriggerDecision. Policy supports: - multi-window evaluation (short + long windows; initial implementation supports per-signal window sizing and an aggregate decision window), - per-signal thresholds for entering/exiting degraded and failed states, - hysteresis via separate enter/exit thresholds, - hold-down timers/cooldowns per region + per target state, - minimum evidence: N-out-of-M samples or consecutive duration before asserting state.

2) Initial config schema + validation: Added a typed config schema (YAML -> struct) for trigger policy with validation + defaults. Config is versioned (schemaVersion: v1) and includes an explicit "monitorOnly" knob. Validation failures block enabling the engine (and emit a structured error).

3) Feature flag + wiring (monitor-only): - Feature flag: failover.trigger_engine.enabled (default false) - Mode flag: failover.trigger_engine.monitor_only (default true when enabled in non-prod; must be explicitly set false later when orchestration lands). When enabled, we compute decisions and emit metrics/logs, but do not change routing or DNS.

4) Metrics + debug logging: - trigger_engine_decision_total{region, decision_state, reason_code} - trigger_engine_signal_value{region, signal} (sampled) - trigger_engine_hold_down_active{region, target_state} Debug log includes signal values used in decision, thresholds, window, and hold-down status. Output is structured so it can be persisted as an audit log in the orchestrator PR (follow-up).

5) Tests: - Unit tests for threshold/hysteresis transitions (enter/exit degraded/failed) - Tests for hold-down behavior (no flappy transitions) - Config validation tests (missing required fields, invalid windows, bad threshold ordering) - Snapshot evaluation tests with synthetic time series covering "noisy p95" and "brief 5xx spike" cases.

Non-goals / Not included: - No orchestration / no routing policy writes / no DNS updates (those land in the orchestrator PR). - No dependency gating or capacity checks (safe-to-failover checks are separate). - No persistence layer for decisions yet; this only emits metrics/logs.

Implementation notes: - New package: internal/failover/triggerengine - Primary types: TriggerPolicy, SignalPolicy, RegionHealthSnapshot, TriggerDecision - Decision format is intentionally explicit for auditability: {target_state, reasons[], evaluated_at, hold_down_until, inputs{signal->(value, window, thresholds)}}.

Example policy snippet (values illustrative): schemaVersion: v1 regions: - name: us-east-1 decisionWindow: 60s holdDown: {degraded: 10m, failed: 20m} signals: error_rate_5xx: {window: 2m, enterDegraded: 0.02, exitDegraded: 0.01, enterFailed: 0.10, exitFailed: 0.05, minSamples: 3} p99_latency_ms: {window: 5m, enterDegraded: 2500, exitDegraded: 2000, enterFailed: 6000, exitFailed: 4500, minConsecutive: 2m}

Rollout plan: - Ship behind feature flag disabled in prod. - Enable in staging in monitor-only mode and compare decisions against game day expectations. - After signal contract + aggregator ship, enable in prod for monitor-only on a low-risk slice (follow-up release gating).

Operational impact: None when disabled. When enabled (monitor-only), expected overhead is minimal: one evaluation per region per tick, plus a small number of metrics.

Related: - ENG-2844 (trigger evaluation logic) - Upcoming: orchestrator state machine + audit log persistence; safe-to-failover gating; progressive failover.

Commits (high-level): 1) failover/triggerengine: add core evaluator + policy types 2) config: add v1 schema + validation + defaults 3) wiring: add feature flag + monitor-only integration point 4) metrics: add decision + signal metrics 5) tests: add unit + config tests

Changed areas (high-level): - internal/failover/triggerengine/* - internal/failover/config/trigger_policy_v1.go - internal/config/flags.go - internal/metrics/failover_metrics.go - cmd/control-plane/* (wiring for evaluation tick) - test/failover/triggerengine/*

Reviewer discussion (abridged): - Aisha Bello: "We should make sure burn-rate alert windows map to the decision windows; avoid choosing 60s decision windows if SLO alerts are 5m/30m." -> Updated defaults: decisionWindow now defaults to 5m unless explicitly set; added validation warning log when decisionWindow < 2m. - Miles Thornton: "Hold-down should be per target state; and we need to ensure we don’t allow failed->healthy immediately if we bounce." -> Implemented separate hold-down timers per target state and added tests for failed->degraded->healthy transitions respecting hold-down. - Ravi Menon: "Policy needs to be understandable by on-call; can we add reason codes that map to signal + threshold names?" -> Added reason_code enum (e.g., ERR_RATE_ENTER_FAILED, P99_ENTER_DEGRADED, HOLD_DOWN_ACTIVE) and included in metrics labels and structured logs. - Benji Okafor: "Feature flag semantics: enabled should never imply orchestration; we must gate orchestration separately." -> Split into two flags; this PR only introduces enabled + monitor_only and hard-codes the action path to no-op.
